nbe479519504.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tripuri Congress of 1939?
o: Bose defeated Rajendra Prasad in the presidential election.
Bose defeated the Gandhi-backed Pattabhi Sitaramayya by 1,580 votes to 1,377.
A Working Committee deadlock led Bose to resign in April 1939.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad became President after Bose resigned.
nbe479519504.x: Bose defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Tripuri; Rajendra Prasad was not his opponent but became President after Bose resigned.

nindian-history-101-7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the INA?
o: The first INA was formed under Mohan Singh in 1942.
The Red Fort trials began before the Azad Hind Government was proclaimed.
Subhas Bose took command of the INA in July 1943.
The Azad Hind Government was proclaimed on 21 October 1943.
nindian-history-101-7.x: The Red Fort trials began in November 1945, two years after the Azad Hind Government was proclaimed on 21 October 1943.

nindian-history-101-18.s: Which INA officer tried at the Red Fort later married Captain Lakshmi?
nindian-history-101-18.x: Prem Kumar Sehgal married Captain Lakshmi; Shah Nawaz Khan later became a Union minister.

n47cc831fdfb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the INA Defence Committee?
o: Tej Bahadur Sapru was associated with the defence.
Asaf Ali was associated with the defence.
Motilal Nehru appeared as a lawyer in the INA trials.
n47cc831fdfb.x: Motilal Nehru could not appear in the INA trials because he was dead by then; Sapru and Asaf Ali were in the defence.

nindian-history-114-5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Swaraj Party and the Congress Socialist Party were founded in the same year.
The Indian National Liberal Federation was founded in 1918.
The Swaraj Party was founded in 1923.
The Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934.
nindian-history-114-5.x: The Swaraj Party came in 1923 and the Congress Socialist Party in 1934, so they were not founded in the same year.

new.s: In which year was Subhas Chandra Bose selected in the ICS?
new.x: Bose was selected in the ICS in 1920 and resigned it in 1921 to join Congress.

new.s: At which Congress session of 1938 was Subhas Chandra Bose President?
new.x: Bose presided over the Haripura session (Gujarat) in 1938; he was re-elected at Tripuri in 1939.

new.s: The Haripura session of 1938, presided over by Bose, was which session of the Congress?
new.x: Haripura (1938) was the 51st session, where the National Planning Committee was set up.

new.s: Who was the Secretary of the National Planning Committee set up in 1938?
new.x: K.T. Shah was Secretary; Nehru was Chairman of the committee set up under Bose.

new.s: By what vote did Bose defeat Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Tripuri in 1939?
new.x: Bose won by 1,580 votes to 1,377 against the Gandhi-backed Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

new.s: After his resignation, Bose was removed from Congress party positions in:
new.x: Bose resigned in April 1939 and was removed from party positions in August 1939.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Forward Bloc:
1. It was founded by Bose in April 1939 after he resigned the Congress presidency.
2. It was formed as a party wholly outside the Congress.
3. Madduri Annapurnaiah led it in Andhra along with Peta Bapayya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Forward Bloc was meant as a bloc within the Congress to unite radical and left-wing forces, so statement 2 is wrong.

new.s: Madduri Annapurnaiah was jailed for 18 months for which article?
new.x: He was jailed for the article 'Chicharapidugu'; Jai Bharat, Navashakti and Velugu are journals he later edited.

new.s: Bose's escape from Calcutta in January 1941 followed which route?
new.x: Bose escaped via Peshawar, Kabul and Moscow to Berlin.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bose's work in Germany?
o: The Free India Centre was set up in Berlin.
Azad Hind Radio was started in Japan.
The Free Indian Legion was raised from Indian POWs captured by Rommel in North Africa.
new.x: Azad Hind Radio was started in Germany and broadcast from Berlin, not Japan.

new.s: Major Iwaichi Fujiwara, who helped form the first INA, headed:
new.x: Fujiwara headed F-Kikan and worked with Mohan Singh and Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon.

new.s: The first INA under Mohan Singh was formally raised on:
new.x: The first INA was raised on 1 September 1942 from Indian POWs after the fall of Singapore.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rash Behari Bose – Indian Independence League, Japan
Rash Behari Ghosh – Indian Independence League, Japan
Mohan Singh – Rani of Jhansi Regiment
new.x: Rash Behari Bose led the IIL in Japan; Rash Behari Ghosh was a Moderate, and the women's regiment was under Lakshmi Sahgal.

new.s: The INA motto 'Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani' means:
new.x: Ittefaq is Unity, Itmad is Faith and Qurbani is Sacrifice.

new.s: The INA's Imphal-Kohima campaign took place in:
new.x: The Imphal-Kohima campaign was in 1944, when the INA flag was hoisted at Moirang.

new.s: Where was the Provisional Government of Free India proclaimed on 21 October 1943?
new.x: It was proclaimed at Singapore, not Rangoon.

new.s: Under the Azad Hind Government, the Andaman Islands were renamed:
new.x: Andaman became Shaheed Dweep (martyr) and Nicobar became Swaraj Dweep (self-rule).

new.s: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands were handed over to the Azad Hind Government by:
new.x: Japan, not Germany, handed over the islands.

new.s: Bose hoisted the tricolour at Port Blair on:
new.x: Bose hoisted the tricolour at Port Blair on 30 December 1943.

new.s: The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny of 1946 began among the ratings of:
new.x: It began on 18 February 1946 when ratings of HMIS Talwar, Bombay, refused duty.

new.s: The ships at Bombay in the RIN Mutiny surrendered on:
new.x: The mutiny began on 18 February and the Bombay ships surrendered on 23 February 1946.

new.s: The title 'Netaji' was given to Subhas Chandra Bose by:
new.x: 'Netaji' came from the people of Germany; Tagore called him 'Desh Nayak'.

new.s: Who called Subhas Chandra Bose the 'Patriot of patriots'?
new.x: Gandhi called Bose the 'Patriot of patriots'.

new.s: Bose gave the call 'Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi dunga' in:
new.x: Bose gave this call in Burma.

new.s: The parallel government 'Prati Sarkar' during the Quit India Movement was set up at:
new.x: Prati Sarkar was at Satara under Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil.

new.s: Who led the parallel government at Ballia in August 1942?
new.x: Chittu Pandey led the Ballia (UP) parallel government.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of parallel government and place is correctly matched?
new.x: Jatiya Sarkar was at Tamluk (Midnapore); Prati Sarkar was at Satara.

new.s: The AICC passed the Quit India Resolution on 8 August 1942 at:
new.x: The AICC met at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on 8 August 1942.

new.s: After the Quit India Resolution, Gandhi was detained at:
new.x: Gandhi was held at the Aga Khan Palace, Pune; the CWC was held at Ahmednagar Fort.

new.s: Kanaklata Barua, shot at 17 while leading a flag procession in 1942, belonged to:
new.x: Kanaklata Barua was from Assam; Matangini Hazra was from Tamluk, Bengal.

new.s: The Congress Working Committee met at Wardha in 1942 on:
new.x: The Wardha CWC met on 14 July 1942; the AICC met at Bombay on 8 August.

new.s: Which two places in Andhra saw police firings during the Quit India Movement of 1942?
new.x: Tenali and Bhimavaram saw firings in 1942.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra in the national movement:
1. Tenali saw a police firing during the Quit India Movement of 1942.
2. Bhimavaram saw a police firing during the Individual Satyagraha of 1940.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Tenali and Bhimavaram firings both took place in 1942 during Quit India, so statement 2 is wrong.

new.s: Who was the first satyagrahi of the Individual Satyagraha of 1940?
new.x: Vinoba Bhave was the first and Nehru the second individual satyagrahi.

new.s: Who was the second individual satyagrahi in 1940?
new.x: Nehru followed Vinoba Bhave in the Individual Satyagraha.

new.s: The August Offer of 1940 was made by Viceroy:
new.x: Viceroy Linlithgow made the August Offer on 8 August 1940; Congress rejected it.

new.s: Which inquiry concluded that Subhas Chandra Bose did NOT die in the plane crash?
new.x: The Mukherjee Commission (1999) said he did not die in the crash; the government rejected its report in 2006.

new.s: In which year was the Khosla Commission on Bose's death set up?
new.x: The Khosla Commission dates to 1970; Shah Nawaz was 1956 and Mukherjee 1999.

new.s: Which INA officers were tried together in the Red Fort trial of 1945?
o: Prem Kumar Sahgal, Mohan Singh, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon
Prem Kumar Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon
Shah Nawaz Khan, Bhulabhai Desai, Prem Kumar Sahgal
Rashid Ali, Mohan Singh, Shah Nawaz Khan
new.x: Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Dhillon were tried together and became a symbol of unity.

new.s: The INA trials at the Red Fort ran from November 1945 to:
new.x: The trials ran from November 1945 to May 1946.

new.s: INA officer Rashid Ali was given a sentence of:
new.x: Rashid Ali's 7-year sentence sparked protests in Calcutta in February 1946.

new.s: In the INA trials (APPSC 2018), Bhulabhai Desai was:
new.x: Bhulabhai Desai was the lead counsel of the INA Defence Committee, not an accused.

new.s: Who among the following did NOT appear for the defence in the INA trials?
new.x: Jinnah did not appear; Sarat Chandra Bose, K.N. Katju and Nehru were in the defence.

new.s: On 21 November 1945, police fired on a student protest for the INA accused in:
new.x: The Calcutta student protest of 21 November 1945 saw firing that killed two.

new.s: Which parties united in support of the INA accused?
new.x: The Congress, the League and the Communists all backed the accused.

new.s: Protests against Rashid Ali's sentence broke out in Calcutta on:
new.x: The Calcutta protests over Rashid Ali's 7-year sentence came on 11 February 1946.

new.s: The Royal Indian Navy was established in:
new.x: The RIN was established in 1934.

new.s: About how many ships were involved in the RIN revolt of 1946?
new.x: About 20,000 personnel, 78 ships and 20 shore establishments were involved.

new.s: Who persuaded the RIN ratings to surrender in February 1946?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali and the Communists
M.S. Khan and the strike committee
new.x: Patel and Jinnah urged surrender; Aruna Asaf Ali and the Communists backed the revolt.

new.s: Who among the following backed the RIN revolt of 1946?
new.x: Only the Communists and Aruna Asaf Ali backed the revolt; Patel and Jinnah asked for surrender.

new.s: The RIAF strike of January 1946 began at:
new.x: The RIAF strike began at Drigh Road, Karachi, and spread to other stations.

new.s: The Army Signal Corps strike of February 1946 took place at:
new.x: The Signal Corps at Jabalpur struck in February 1946.

new.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the 1945-46 upsurges is correctly matched?
new.x: The post and telegraph strike was in July 1946; the RIAF strike was in January and Jabalpur in February 1946.

new.s: The Indian Army, which the British could no longer trust after 1946, numbered about:
new.x: The 2.5-million Indian Army, the Raj's sword, could no longer be relied on.

new.s: The Cabinet Mission, announced by Attlee on 19 February 1946, arrived in India on:
new.x: Announced on 19 February 1946, the mission arrived on 24 March 1946.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. INA Day
2. RIAF strike at Drigh Road
3. RIN mutiny on HMIS Talwar
4. Attlee announces the Cabinet Mission
new.x: INA Day (12 Nov 1945), RIAF strike (Jan 1946), RIN mutiny (18 Feb 1946), Cabinet Mission announced (19 Feb 1946).

new.s: Who was known as 'Andhra Kesari'?
new.x: Prakasam earned the title 'Andhra Kesari' in the Simon boycott in Madras.

new.s: The title 'Deshabhakta' belongs to:
new.x: Konda Venkatappayya was 'Deshabhakta'; C.R. Das was 'Deshbandhu'.

new.s: Who was called 'Bihar Kesari'?
new.x: Bihar Kesari was Sri Krishna Sinha; Bharatha Kesari was Mannathu Padmanabhan.

new.s: Who is known as 'Loknayak'?
new.x: Jayaprakash Narayan is called Loknayak.

new.s: 'Frontier Gandhi' Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan founded the:
new.x: He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Red Shirts) in November 1929; the Khaksars were founded by Mashriqui.

new.s: Who is called the 'Socrates of Maharashtra'?
new.x: Gokhale, Gandhi's political mentor, is the 'Socrates of Maharashtra' (APPSC 2025).

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Deshbandhu was C.R. Das; Deen Bandhu was C.F. Andrews, Andhra Ratna was Duggirala and Kerala Gandhi was K. Kelappan.

new.s: 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936) was written by:
new.x: Ambedkar wrote 'Annihilation of Caste' in 1936.

new.s: 'Feathers and Stones' was written by:
new.x: 'Feathers and Stones' is by Pattabhi, not Sarojini Naidu.

new.s: 'A National Flag for India' (1916) was written by:
new.x: Pingali Venkayya wrote 'A National Flag for India' in 1916.

new.s: Which of the following about Gandhi's writings is NOT correct?
o: Hind Swaraj is his Gujarati rendering of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last'.
Sarvodaya is his Gujarati rendering of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last'.
Songs from Prison was written in Yerwada Prison in 1932.
Hind Swaraj is his own original book.
new.x: Hind Swaraj is Gandhi's own book; the rendering of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' is Sarvodaya.

new.s: Who compared the Dandi March to Napoleon's return from Elba?
new.x: Subhas Bose compared the Dandi March to Napoleon's return from Elba.

new.s: 'Sedition has become my religion' was said at Dandi by:
new.x: Gandhi said this at Dandi; 'Swaraj is my birthright' was Tilak's.

new.s: Abhinav Bharat (1904) was founded by:
new.x: Abhinav Bharat was founded by Savarkar, not Bose.

new.s: The Muslim League was founded in 1906 at:
new.x: The Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dhaka, not in 1918.

new.s: The Independent Labour Party (1936) was founded by:
new.x: Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party in 1936.

new.s: The Social Service League (1911, Bombay) was founded by:
new.x: N.M. Joshi, a follower of Gokhale, founded it to run schools, libraries and dispensaries for Bombay workers.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of person and organisation is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru – Independence for India League
Motilal Nehru – Servants of India Society
new.x: The Servants of India Society was founded by Gokhale, not Motilal Nehru (APPSC 2024).

new.s: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded by Gandhi in:
new.x: Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932, with branches at Hyderabad and Vijayawada.

new.s: Who was the first Indian President of the Central Legislative Assembly?
new.x: Vithalbhai Patel was elected on 24 August 1925 after Sir Frederick Whyte.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Vithalbhai Patel:
1. He was elected President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925 after Sir Frederick Whyte.
2. In 1928 he secured a separate office for the Assembly, independent of the government.
3. He set the convention that the President leads the government side in debates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: He set the convention that the President stays neutral in debates, so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: Who presided over the Lahore session of the Congress in 1929?
new.x: Nehru, not Gandhi, presided at Lahore in 1929.

new.s: Who is known as the 'Builder of modern Assam'?
new.x: Gopinath Bordoloi is called the Builder of modern Assam.

new.s: K. Kelappan, the 'Kerala Gandhi', is associated with the:
new.x: Kelappan led the Guruvayur satyagraha; Vedaranyam was Rajagopalachari's march.

new.s: Poet-revolutionary Kesari Singh Barahath belonged to:
new.x: Kesari Singh Barahath was from Shahpura, Rajasthan.

new.s: Who was the first queen to wage war against the British (1780)?
new.x: Velu Nachiyar of Sivaganga was the first queen to fight the British, in 1780.

new.s: Bhikaiji Cama first hoisted the Indian flag abroad at:
new.x: Cama hoisted the flag at Stuttgart in 1907.

new.s: Who hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942 and went underground?
new.x: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank; Cama's flag was abroad at Stuttgart.

new.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded Andhra Bank in:
new.x: Pattabhi founded Andhra Bank in 1923 and Andhra Insurance in 1925.

new.s: The present national flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
new.x: The flag, with the Ashoka Chakra in place of the charkha, was adopted on 22 July 1947.

new.s: Komaram Bheem led the movement of the:
new.x: Komaram Bheem led the Gond movement (1938-44) with the slogan 'Jal-Jangal-Zameen'.

new.s: Birsa Munda's movement in Chotanagpur is known as:
new.x: Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan.

new.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju's Rampa rebellion was supported by which tribals?
new.x: The Rampa rebellion (1922-24) drew on Koya and Jatapu tribals.

new.s: N.G. Ranga, who resigned his professorship in 1930, is associated with:
new.x: N.G. Ranga led the Andhra kisan movement; the Bihar Kisan Sabha was Sahajanand's.
